_comment: SANITRAC TMS-V1.2 gas sensor calibration reference. See docs/gas-sensors-research.md.

_correction_factor_constants.source: MQ-135 derived fit; approximate for MQ-2/4/9/137 - refit from fleet data

MQ137.purpose: Ammonia from urea hydrolysis - the dominant toilet odorant. Primary cleanliness channel.

notes: Datasheet sensitivity line reads 'Rs(air)/Rs(5000ppm CH4)>=5' - copy-paste error from MQ-2.
Smoke: 10 cigarettes in 8 m^3 room produces output equal to 10 ppm NH3. Smoking WILL look like ammonia.

curve.warning: Published library fits use log-log slope ~-0.264, but the datasheet alpha<=0.6 spec requires |slope|>=0.737 - off by ~3x. Sources also disagree on intercept (+0.42 vs -0.241, giving 39 ppm vs 0.12 ppm for the same input). Do NOT ship ppm from these. Use the odour index, or calibrate against a reference instrument.

MQ137.threshold_basis: NIOSH REL TWA 25 ppm, STEL 35 ppm; measured restroom NH3 3.16-6.88 ppm; reported urine odour 10-40 ppm

MQ2.purpose: Aerosol propellant, cleaning chemicals, tobacco smoke, LPG. Event and cleaning-verification channel.

curve.warning: Derived from library fits of the datasheet curve image, not from the datasheet text. Do not treat MQ-2 CO as a real CO measurement - use MQ-9 for that.

MQ2.threshold_basis: propane LEL 2.1% = 21000 ppm; 5000 ppm is roughly 10-25% LEL depending on gas

MQ4.purpose: Sewer gas ingress, dry trap, septic backflow. Also corroborates faecal odour.

datasheet.datasheet_calibration_advice: calibrate at 5000 ppm CH4 with RL ~20k
notes: Small sensitivity to alcohol and smoke - cleaner CH4 channel than MQ-2.

MQ4.threshold_basis: CH4 LEL = 5% = 50000 ppm. 5000 ppm = 10% LEL (standard industrial alarm), 10000 ppm = 20% LEL.

MQ9.purpose: Carbon monoxide from nearby generators/geysers/vehicle exhaust. Excluded from the odour index.

datasheet.load_resistance_note: adjustable; 10k used for the datasheet curve

MQ9.heater_cycle_warning: CO is only valid during the 1.4 V low-temperature phase. If the TMS-V1.2 heater is hard-tied to 5 V, MQ-9 CO readings are NOT carbon monoxide - publish nothing, or label it as a second combustible-gas channel. HARDWARE CONFIRMATION REQUIRED.

sampling.co_sample_window: last ~10 s of the 90 s low phase
sampling.combustible_sample_window: last ~10 s of the 60 s high phase

MQ9.threshold_basis: EPA 8h IAQ 9 ppm; NIOSH REL TWA 35 ppm, ceiling 200 ppm, IDLH 1200 ppm; OSHA PEL 50 ppm

odour_index.baseline_source: rolling 7-day low percentile of Rs_corrected, re-anchored on RFID-verified cleaning events
overrides: MQ-4 > 10% LEL (5000 ppm) or MQ-2 sustained high -> independent safety alarm path, no averaging delay
any sensor open/short/out-of-range -> FAULT state, never 'clean'
RFID cleaner scan -> odour alarm hold-off window

power_budget_5v.warning: HLK-PM01 is 3 W / 600 mA and would be undersized. Recommend HLK-10M05 (10 W) or 12 W class plus bulk capacitance. A sagging 5 V rail changes Vc and corrupts every gas reading. CONFIRM PART NUMBER.

unknowns_blocking_firmware: ADC divider resistor values per channel (needed to recover V_RL from V_adc)
RL value fitted per sensor on the shield
ESP32-S3 GPIO assignment per gas channel (ADC1 = GPIO1-10 only; ADC2 unusable with WiFi)
MQ-9 heater switchable or hard-tied 5 V
